source_text:
Οὐδέν μοι ὠφελήσει τὰ πέρατα τοῦ κόσμου οὐδὲ αἱ βασιλεῖαι τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου. καλόν μοι ἀποθανεῖν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν, ἢ βασιλεύειν τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς. ἐκεῖνον ζητῶ, τὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἀποθανόντα: ἐκεῖνον θέλω, τὸν δἰ ἡμᾶς ἀναστάντα. ὁ δὲ τοκετός μοι ἐπίκειται.
σύγγνωτέ μοι, ἀδελφοί: μὴ ἐμποδίσητέ μοι ζῆσαι, μὴ θελήσητε με ἀποθανεῖν: τὸν τοῦ θεοῦ θέλοντα εἶναι κόσμῳ μὴ χαρίσησθε, μηδὲ ὕλῃ ἐξαπατήσητε: ἄφετέ με καθαρὸν φῶς λαβεῖν: ἐκεῖ παραγενόμενος ἄνθρωπος ἔσομαι.
ἐπιτρέψατέ μοι μιμητὴν εἶναι τοῦ πάθους τοῦ θεοῦ μου. εἴ τις αὐτὸν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔχει, νοησάτω ὃ θέλω, καὶ συμπαθείτω μοι εἰδὼς τὰ συνέχοντά με.
thought_title: Death is gain, not the world
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the church in Rome while being taken under guard to martyrdom there, and he is urging them not to prevent his death.
pass_a_gloss: Nothing will profit me the ends of the world nor the kingdoms of this age. [It is] good for me to die into Christ Jesus, rather than to reign [over] the ends of the earth. That one I seek, the [one] on behalf of us having died; that one I want, the [one] through us having risen. But the birth pangs lie upon me. Forgive me, brothers; do not hinder me to live, do not wish me to die; the [one] of God wishing to be, to the world do not give [him] as a favor, nor by matter deceive [him]; let me receive pure light; there having arrived, a human being I will be. Permit me to be an imitator of the passion of my God. If anyone him in himself has, let him understand what I want, and let him suffer with me, knowing the [things] constraining me.

choices.why: The preposition εἰς with a person expresses movement into union with Christ; rendering it as 'into' preserves the spatial force that 'for' would lose.
The noun refers to the pains of childbirth; 'birth pangs' keeps the concrete physical sense Ignatius uses for his coming martyrdom.

choices.english: the one who wants to belong to God
choices.why: The participle θέλοντα with the genitive τοῦ θεοῦ means 'the one wishing to be God's'; 'belong to God' makes the possessive force clear in English.
rejected: the one of God wishing to be

choices.why: The dative ὕλῃ denotes the material realm as opposed to the pure light Ignatius seeks; 'matter' keeps the philosophical contrast sharp.

choices.english: I will be a human being
choices.why: Ignatius contrasts his present constrained state with becoming fully human at death; the bare noun with the future copula carries that force.
The verb συμπαθέω means to share in suffering or feeling; 'suffer with me' preserves the prefix συν- and the emotional solidarity Ignatius requests.

pass_b_english: The ends of the world and the kingdoms of this age will profit me nothing. It is better for me to die into Christ Jesus than to reign over the ends of the earth. I seek the one who died for us; I want the one who rose for us. The pangs of my birth are upon me.

Forgive me, brothers and sisters: do not hinder me from living, do not wish me to die. Do not hand over to the world the one who wants to belong to God, and do not deceive him with worldly things. Let me receive pure light; when I arrive there, I will be a human being.
Allow me to be an imitator of the passion of my God. If anyone has him within himself, let him understand what I want, and let him suffer with me, knowing what constrains me.

last_rejected.quote: do not wish me to die
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'do not wish me to die,' but context demands 'do not wish my death' as ironic paradox with 'living.'
last_rejected.ruling: μὴ θελήσητε με ἀποθανεῖν literally means 'do not wish me to die'; rendering is accurate, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: and do not deceive me with matter
last_rejected.why: Dative ὕλῃ is instrumental 'by matter,' not 'with matter' as accompaniment; 'deceive by matter' means material world.
last_rejected.fix: and do not deceive me by matter
last_rejected.ruling: 'with matter' correctly renders instrumental dative ὕλῃ; no meaningful distinction from 'by matter' here.

polish.changed: Clarified the paradox of living and dying by keeping Ignatius's exact wording but smoothing the sentence flow, replaced vague 'matter' with 'worldly things' to match the Greek sense, and preserved the birth-pangs metaphor as Ignatius's own voice without adding explanation.

notes.why: 'Passible' (capable of suffering) vs 'passion' (suffering/death) are related but distinct; reader may miss Christological point.
notes.fix: Gloss 'passible' as 'capable of suffering' on first use.

notes.quote: The birth pangs are upon me
notes.why: Metaphor unclear whose voice this is; Pauline allusion (Gal 4:19) unexplained.
notes.fix: Note: adapts Paul's labor-pains metaphor for spiritual formation.

notes.quote: Do not hinder me from living, do not wish me to die
notes.why: Paradox garbled: asks not to be hindered from 'living' (in Christ) but also not wished to die—reader may think this contradicts 'I want to die'.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'living' means true life in Christ, which death achieves.

notes.quote: do not deceive me with matter
notes.why: 'Matter' is vague; the Greek likely means 'worldly things' or 'material things,' not philosophical 'matter.'
notes.fix: Use 'material things' or 'the things of this world.'

polish.changed: Clarified the birth metaphor as 'the pangs of my birth' so readers see Ignatius speaking of his death as a birth into true life, and kept the speaker and pronouns explicit throughout.

notes.quote: The birth pangs are upon me
notes.why: Metaphor of death as childbirth is biblical, but 'birth pangs' for dying may confuse; reader expects birth, not death.
notes.fix: Add note: 'biblical metaphor for suffering that precedes new life/resurrection.'

problems.quote: Do not hand over to the world the one who wants to belong to God, and do not deceive me with worldly things.
problems.why: Second clause 'do not deceive me' seems to belong to different sentence; abrupt shift from third to first person.
problems.fix: Punctuate as new sentence or revise: 'Do not deceive me by offering me worldly things.'

edits.old: Do not hand over to the world the one who wants to belong to God, and do not deceive me with worldly things.
edits.new: Do not hand over to the world the one who wants to belong to God, and do not deceive him with worldly things.

fixed: The second clause 'do not deceive me' was corrected to 'do not deceive him' to match the source, which continues the third-person object from the previous clause.
